There aren’t any emergency plumbers available through my system right now for your address, so I can’t directly book someone. I can still help you handle this and quickly find a local plumber.

1) Limit damage right now  
- If it’s safe: look under the sink for two small shutoff valves on the pipes (hot/cold). Turn both clockwise until they stop; that usually stops water to the faucet and the leak.  
- If there are no under-sink valves, you may need to shut off the main water valve to the house (often near where the water line enters the house or by an outside wall/garage).  
- Put a bucket or pan under the leak and move anything that can be damaged by water. Put towels down to soak up standing water.

2) How to quickly find an emergency plumber near you  
On your phone or computer, search:  
“emergency plumber near me” or “emergency plumber Fort Worth 76102”

Then:
- Filter for places that:  
  - Are “Open now” or list 24/7 or emergency service  
  - Have around 4★+ rating and a solid number of reviews  
- Call the top 2–3 options and ask:  
  - “Can you send someone for an emergency leak under a kitchen sink at 1234 Main Street, Fort Worth, TX 76102 today?”  
  - “How soon can they get here?”  
  - “What is your emergency service call fee and a rough cost range if it’s just a pipe/fitting under the sink?”

3) Info to give them  
- Address: 1234 Main Street, Fort Worth, TX 76102  
- Issue: “Water leaking under the kitchen sink; single-family home; water is currently [on/off]”  
- Priority: “Earliest possible arrival today.”

If you tell me whether you’ll mostly be calling or texting plumbers, I can write a short script you can read on the phone or paste into a text with all your details included.</action>
